article.title: Schumer & Jeffries reap the backlash to the genocide they enabled
article.author: Zoe Alexandra
article.content: Democrats just flipped Congress in a landslide, turned Texas blue, and won a Kansas Senate seat for the first time in nearly a century. But as Rania Khalek explains, the leaders of the new majority on Capitol Hill are the same “corporate suits” who armed Israel through the genocide in Gaza before losing to Trump in 2024, backing record ICE funding through 2029, and sitting on their hands while the administration tore the country and the world apart. Khalek lays out how midterm voters delivered a massive rebuke to Trump’s war on Iran, ICE terror, and soaring cost of living, electing insurgent progressives across the country. But Chuck Schumer insists “the issue is not me,” as Abdul El-Sayed, Troy Jackson and Adam Hamilton say they won’t back him for majority leader. And presumptive House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries thinks when it comes to holding Trump administration officials accountable, Americans “don’t want us to get even.” So what will Democrats actually do with this mandate? Will they investigate and prosecute MAGA crimes, cut off war funding, and break with AIPAC? Or will leadership smother the insurgent wave before it even reaches Washington? “I am absolutely elated – but I’m also cringing because people like Chuck Schumer are reaping the benefits of the backlash to Trump after taking zero accountability for the horrors their party unleashed.” Watch full episodes of BT Live, join breakthroughnews.org as a member today! #breakthroughnews ****** Rough transcript follows: Democrats won the Senate with 54 seats to 44 seats, and we’re still waiting on Alaska and Mississippi. Democrats are leading in both, so we’ll see how that turns out. They also took the House with 240 seats called so far, and NBC projects they’ll end up around 258 seats, which is a supermajority. Even Texas turned blue, indicating a massive mandate. The question is, what will they do with that mandate? While it’s satisfying to see certain figures defeated, there’s concern about leaders like Chuck Schumer, who still support war and genocide, benefiting from the backlash to Trump without taking accountability for past actions. The corporate Democratic leadership started a genocide in Gaza, lost to fascists, and did little while Trump caused chaos. Now, they’re trying to claim this backlash as a victory, but they’re still quite disliked. This election was also a rejection of them, as many Democratic insurgent candidates won across the country. The point is, this is not the time to relax. It’s time to get organized because leaders like Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries may try to obstruct significant changes. The mainstream media is already trying to discipline and tame the more progressive winners of this election. For example, CNN asked James Talarico, now a senator-elect in Texas, if he’ll stand up to the Democrats in Washington. [Speaker 2:] “I will stand up to anyone I have to, to defend the people of Texas. I will work with anyone I can to help the people of Texas. This is what I’ve done for four terms in the state house, long before the Senate race and before doing interviews on CNN.” As for Schumer, when asked about new Democrats who want him out as leader, he said: [Speaker 3:] “The issue is not me. I’ll be reelected as majority leader. The issue is focusing on the American people and what they want.” Some Democrats are ready for a fight. Robert Garcia, about to chair the House Oversight Committee, has vowed to take on the Trump crime family, corporate corruption, ICE, DHS abuses, and the Epstein coverups. He released a statement with two words: “Lawyer up,” speaking directly to Trump. However, Hakeem Jeffries, expected to become Speaker of the House, said: [Speaker 4:] “The American people don’t want us to get even. They want us to get things done on their behalf because life is way too expensive. We ran on affordability, won on affordability, and now it’s our job to govern on affordability.” This attitude is not surprising from Jeffries, who is a major recipient of corporate PAC money and pro-Israel lobby funds. He has been an ardent supporter of Israeli actions, even during conflicts like Operation Protective Edge in 2014. Let’s listen to a clip of him during a pro-Israel rally: [Speaker 5:] “Israel faced aggression in 1948 and prevailed. In 1967, Israel prevailed. In 1973, Israel prevailed. During the first and second intifadas, Israel prevailed. Missiles flew in 2008 and 2012, and Israel prevailed. I’m confident we’ll stand together: Israel today, Israel tomorrow, Israel forever.” This phrasing echoes segregationist George Wallace’s infamous quote. Yet, progressive Democrats like AOC and Brad Lander insist on voting for Jeffries as speaker without conditions. Zoran, who isn’t even in Congress, is pushing for him as well. We’ll see what insurgent Democrats like Claire Valdez and others do. If they let Jeffries become speaker, little will change. A petition circulating online has over 500,000 signatures to appoint someone more progressive than Jeffries as speaker. Chuck Schumer also supports the genocide in Gaza. Here’s what he said about Palestinians: [Speaker 6:] “The view of Palestinians is simple: Europeans treated Jews badly, culminating in the Holocaust, and gave them our land as compensation. We say it’s our land; the Torah says it, but they don’t believe in the Torah. That’s why there’s no peace. We must stand strong with Israel through thick and thin.” This statement is problematic. Schumer calls himself the guardian of Israel and has built his career around protecting it in Congress. He should not be the Democratic leader in the Senate. Some Senate Democrats, like Adam Hamilton and others, oppose him, but he claims he has the majority support needed. Corporate figures like Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer represent what the Democratic Party stands for now. In Israel, there’s panic, but not everyone is worried. Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid tweeted: [Speaker 7:] “Hakeem Jeffries will lead the House. Chuck Schumer will run the Senate. Both are my friends and voted with Israel this year. They’re leaders Israel should work with, even if we don’t agree on everything. The anti-Israel core in the House has grown, but it’s a small minority.” Only 13% of Democrats have a positive view of Israel, yet this minority runs the party. AIPAC bragged that more than 234 candidates supported by its members have won. This party won’t voluntarily give people what they want. They govern for the ruling class, not for us. Their leadership opposes universal healthcare, capping prescription drug prices, taxing billionaires, cutting off Israel, and ending wars. We need to build outside this decrepit Republican-lite party, or we’ll stay stuck in a cycle of liberal to fascist until it’s just fascist.
